extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics. The dataset was crowdsourced using a two-step process leveraging study textbooks, a rule-based document filter, and a machine learning model to suggest distractors.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected via a two-step crowdsourcing workflow on Amazon Mechanical Turk. First, crowd workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs and asked to select one (or reject all) to formulate an in-domain question and answer. Second, another worker validated the question and selected up to two machine-generated distractor options and authored at least one distractor to yield three distractors per question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 science textbooks from online learning resources including CK-12 and OpenStax covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics from elementary level to college introductory material.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Paragraphs from the base corpus were filtered using a rule-based sentence classifier that accepts a paragraph if a minimum number of sentences pass. Rules filtered out sentences with questions, exclamations, lack of verb phrases, modal verbs, imperative phrases, demonstrative pronouns, non-third-person personal pronouns, pronoun sentence starters, first names, length outside 6-18 tokens, more than two commas, non-punctuation special characters, more than three uppercase tokens, mentions of graphs/tables/links, discourse markers, absolute wording, or instructional vocabulary.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: In the first task, crowd workers selected a textbook passage and wrote a question (6-30 words) and answer (up to 3 words) querying general principles. In the second task, workers reviewed the question-answer pair, checked if it could appear on a school science exam (filtering out ungrammatical, incorrect, unrelated, or overly specific questions), chose up to two model-suggested distractors, and authored at least one distractor.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 92.8% of generated questions passed worker validation in the second task. 36.1% of final distractors were chosen from model suggestions. In a qualitative evaluation, humans distinguished crowdsourced questions from real exam questions in only 55% of cases (p > 0.05). Human performance on a sample of 650 questions across 13 annotators was 87.8% +/- 0.045.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 175 Amazon Mechanical Turk crowd workers with Master's status.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: scikit-learn Random Forest classifier (for distractor ranking)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A small percentage of passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, reducing the size of the direct-answer version to 10,481 train, 887 dev, and 884 test instances. Machine-suggested distractors occasionally suffered from misalignment in level of specificity or ungrammaticality for multiword expressions, requiring crowd worker filtering.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for multiple choice and direct answer question answering / reading comprehension models; augmenting training data for school science exam question answering.
